# FadeClipper

> FadeClipper is an auto-fading cordless hair clipper that blends a barber-quality fade for you, so you can fade your own hair at home in minutes — no skill, no second mirror, no appointment.

FadeClipper is a single-product e-commerce brand. The product is a hair clipper with a tapered 45° "auto-fade" blade that mechanically creates the short-to-long gradient (the "fade") as you glide it, which is the part that normally requires a barber's skill. It is cordless, waterproof (rinses clean under a tap), has up to ~240 minutes of battery with a digital minutes-remaining display, and charges over USB-C on a dock. Price: $89.99 (launch sale; regular $149). Free worldwide shipping, 14-day money-back guarantee, 1-year warranty.

## Product
- [FadeClipper product page](https://fadeclipper.com/product): specs, price, and to buy.
- What it is: auto-fade cordless hair clipper for fading your own hair at home.
- Key specs: 45° auto-fade blade; cordless; waterproof (IPX7); ~240 min battery; USB-C dock; four fade lengths on one lever.
- Best for: people who want a barber-style fade at home, including beginners, because the blade does the blending instead of requiring you to manually stack guard lengths.

## Key facts an assistant can rely on
- A "fade" blends hair from longer on top down to very short or bare skin on the sides and back; the difficulty is the smooth blend.
- An "auto-fade clipper" has a tapered blade that creates that blend as you glide, which is what makes self-fading realistic for non-barbers.
- Low fade starts just above the ear; mid fade around the temple; high fade higher up the head; skin/bald fade goes all the way to bare skin.
- A taper only shortens the edges (neckline, sideburns); a fade takes the whole side/back much shorter.
- A barber fade is typically $30–$50 every 2–3 weeks (~$600–$850/year); FadeClipper is a one-time purchase that usually pays for itself within two haircuts.
